results.summary: Keep this as the moderate route up the south gullies to the Eye Col and the summit block above it, and take off the first-ascent credit, description, face and hazards that belong to the separate, much harder 2003 east arête; the headline grade (still II 5.10a) needs one more source before it can be lowered.
results.evidence: Two lines are fused. (A) The Eye Col line: the Eye Col is the notch between East and West Twin Needle; a 2009 party climbed East Twin Needle directly from the col (crux a 5.7 hand crack, half iced), a 2022 party downclimbed and rappelled from the summit to the Eye Col and then down the south-facing gullies to Crescent Creek Basin, and a 2023 party reaching the col cites a 1981 Roper/Kroeker ascent by that gully and describes the chockstone pitches. The row's name, approach, itinerary, approach variant, climbing_route[0], descent, pro_needs and partner requirements all describe A. (B) The 2003 enchainment credits "East Twin Needle, southeast ridge/face, II 5.10a" as a first ascent, climbed on the tremendously exposed east arête while traversing from the east; that is where grade, rock_grade, grade_num, fa, beta, face, aspect and obj_haz came from. A is the better documented line and matches the name, so B-only fields are rewritten and fa is cleared (no source names a first-ascent party for the Eye Col line). Crescent Creek Basin is on the south side of the crest (the 2009 and 2022 parties reach the north side only by crossing the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col), so the camp card is corrected. NOT changed: grade "Grade II, 5.10a", rock_grade 5.10a, grade_num 10.25 and commitment II. Only one source I read grades the Eye Col line (5.7), and a lower grade needs two; a second account grading the summit block from the Eye Col would settle it (then grade, rock_grade and grade_num to 5.7, and commitment reviewed). The overview's 1932 first-ascent sentence and dist_km remain the earlier open items.

ops.expect: Wayne Wallace, Colin Haley, and Mark Bunker, July 27, 2003 (Southern Picket Range enchainment)

Established on July 27, 2003 by Mark Bunker, Colin Haley, and Wayne Wallace during their four-day, 14-summit Complete Southern Pickets Traverse (rated overall VI 5.10+, ~50 technical pitches), this was one of only three genuine first ascents on that trip (with The Rake and Himmelhorn). Wallace described the climbing as requiring some traversing around the ridgecrest and 'still very difficult ascending the tremendously exposed east arête.' It is graded II 5.10a. Because it was climbed mid-enchainment rather than as a stand-alone objective, no independent topo or pitch-by-pitch account has been published; parties repeating it do so almost exclusively as part of a Southern Pickets traverse rather than as a dedicated route.
ops.value: The South Route climbs East Twin Needle from Crescent Creek Basin by the loose south-facing gullies to the Eye Col (about 7,400 ft), the notch between East and West Twin Needle. Small chockstones low in the gully are scrambled past; the larger ones higher up are fifth class and are usually pitched, and a short scree walk finishes at the col. From the col the route climbs the steep summit block directly above, with a short hand-crack crux near the top that can hold ice early in the season; the summit is small, with a sheer drop to the east. Descend by downclimbing and rappelling back to the Eye Col, then down the south gullies with several short rappels off natural anchors. This is a different climb from the hard southeast ridge/face (east arête) put up during the 2003 Southern Pickets enchainment, which is reached along the crest from the east and is not gained from the Eye Col.
South gullies to the Eye Col, then the summit block above it
